releaseNotice: WakeSharp 2.25 is live on the App Store. Google Play has version 2.9, so some features described here are iPhone-only for now. Get the latest update from the App Store or Google Play.
hero: Pick a sound from the Loud category, then choose what you want to do when the alarm rings. Solve a few math problems, scan a bottle, or get moving with a walking mission.
loudTitle: Start with a sound you will notice
loud: Loud is a sound category in the alarm editor. Open the sound picker, listen to the tones, and choose the one you want for that alarm. You can pair the same tone with any available mission.
volume: On iPhone, system alarm volume is controlled by iOS. Choosing a Loud tone does not override that setting. On Android, check the alarm volume and allow alarms in Do Not Disturb. Test the sound on your own phone before relying on it.
scanTitle: Get up. Find it. Scan it.
scan: Choose a target such as a bottle, mug or sink. When the alarm rings, point the camera at that object. The green match confirmation tells you when WakeSharp has recognised it. Object recognition runs on your phone.
missionsIntro: Choose from the missions below, or put up to four in a sequence. This is the iPhone 2.25 selection; Google Play has version 2.9, so Squats and Push-ups are iPhone-only for now. Camera, movement and voice missions need their corresponding permissions and supported hardware.
hubTitle: Alarm missions that give you a reason to get up
hubDescription: Explore WakeSharp alarm missions, loud tones, group alarms, calendar alarms and shift rotations. Choose a task that fits your morning and see how it works.
englishArtwork: The screenshots are in English. The captions describe each screen in your language.
watch: On iPhone, tapping “I’m up” on Apple Watch delays the phone alarm by one minute. Finish the mission on your iPhone to stop the repeat alarms. The Watch needs to be charged, connected and set up.
android: WakeSharp is also on Google Play, where version 2.9 is the current release. Its alarm stream, permissions and battery settings differ from iPhone, and it does not include the newer iPhone features named on this page: Squats, Push-ups, group alarms and the 30-second repeat. These images show iPhone and Apple Watch, not Android or Wear OS. Check the installed app for the missions and controls available on your platform.
backup: No WakeSharp account is required, except for group alarms. Optional sign-in with Apple or Google backs up alarms, history, preferences and small photo-target thumbnails. Camera matching and calendar processing happen on your device. Calendar event content stays there. Read the privacy policy for the full details.
deleting: Uninstalling removes local app data, but does not delete an optional cloud backup or cancel a store subscription. Delete the backup through Settings → Account → Delete account, or use the account deletion page. Manage your subscription separately in the store.
score: Sharpness is a daily in-app score. Review it under Achievements alongside your history, streaks and badges, then visit Nest for your progress with Lark. It is not a sleep score or a medical assessment. A single number does not tell you whether you are safe to drive or work.
warmup: Your Sharpness Score comes from the missions you finish when the alarm rings. The separate brain warm-up is not offered in the current app. Math Problems, Memory Match and Sequence Recall are alarm missions.
developer: I’m Dipojjal, the developer behind WakeSharp. I build it at KineticBit. I want the app to be clear about what it can do and what depends on your phone. If something is confusing or an alarm misbehaves, the contact form reaches me.
repeat: On iPhone, stop it or snooze it and it rings again within 30 seconds, until your mission is done. Google Play’s version 2.9 rings again a minute later, for up to an hour. Your phone’s own controls still work.

features: Loud alarm tones
Choose a sound from the Loud category for an alarm that stands out. Check volume and permissions on your iPhone or Android phone.
Open an alarm and its sound picker. Select the Loud category.
Preview a tone and save it to that alarm. Choose a mission separately.
Set a short test alarm. Check your phone’s volume, permissions and battery.
Scan an Object alarm
Scan a real object when your alarm rings. Choose a bottle, mug or sink, point the camera at it, and look for the green match confirmation.
Choose Scan an Object in the mission picker and select a target.
Put the target somewhere you can reach safely after getting up.
Point the camera at it in good light. Hold it steady until the match turns green.
Math alarm clock
WakeSharp’s Math Problems mission asks you to solve arithmetic when the alarm rings. Choose a difficulty you can finish in the morning.
Choose Math Problems in your alarm’s mission picker.
Set the difficulty and try it while you are awake. Start with a manageable challenge.
When the alarm rings, enter the correct answers to finish the rounds.
Puzzle alarm clock
Choose memory, sequence or colour challenges for your morning alarm. WakeSharp lets you set a puzzle mission or combine several tasks.
Choose Memory Match, Sequence Recall or Color Clash.
Try the difficulty before saving. A harder puzzle is not always a better alarm.
Find the card pairs, repeat the pattern, or tap the ink colour when the alarm rings.
Photo alarm clock
Photo Proof asks you to retake a reference photo. Compare it with object scanning, Fetch and other WakeSharp camera missions.
Choose Photo Proof and take a clear reference photo of your chosen spot.
Use a spot with stable lighting and recognisable details, such as a shelf.
Return and frame the same spot when the alarm rings. Scan an Object is a separate mission for recognising an object category.
Walking and exercise alarm clock
Walk It Off counts real steps during your alarm mission. First Light asks for daylight. On iPhone, Squats and Push-ups count your reps with the camera.
Choose Walk It Off and allow the motion permission it needs, or choose Squats or Push-ups on iPhone and allow the camera.
Try a short route with your phone in your hand or pocket. Check that steps register. For Push-ups, lay the phone on the floor and let the front camera count.
Walk carefully when the alarm rings. First Light instead asks you to hold your phone in daylight.
Calendar alarm clock
Set a WakeSharp alarm before your first calendar event, with an earliest and latest wake time. Calendar processing stays on your device.
Allow calendar access and create a calendar alarm.
Choose how many minutes before the event to ring, plus the earliest and latest times.
Review the next alarm after editing your calendar. Keep a fixed backup for an appointment you cannot miss.
Alarm clock for shift workers
Build an alarm rotation around your shifts instead of a seven-day week. Preview upcoming dates and skip a day without deleting the pattern.
Create a shift rotation and choose its starting date.
Add work and rest phases with the alarm time for each working phase.
Check the preview calendar against your roster. Skip individual dates when your plans change.
WakeSharp Sharpness Score
Review your daily Sharpness Score, your badges and your morning history under Achievements. Follow your own progress without treating it as a medical test.
Finish your morning and open Achievements.
Review the score breakdown shown in the app, and the badges you have earned.
Look at several mornings in your history. Use badges and Nest as encouragement, not as a health diagnosis.
